definitions.explanation: Family descent or hereditary connection passed down through generations. Emphasizes the biological and spiritual continuity of a family line.
A vein or artery carrying blood. A literary or classical usage, less common in modern everyday language.

examples.japanese: {血脈|けつみゃく}を{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ。
{名門|めいもん}の{血脈|けつみゃく}を{引|ひ}いている。
examples.english: He is descended from a distinguished lineage.

examples.japanese: {家族|かぞく}の{血脈|けつみゃく}は{途絶|とだ}えることなく{現代|げんだい}まで{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: The family bloodline has continued unbroken to the present day.

examples.japanese: {全身|ぜんしん}の{血脈|けつみゃく}を{巡|めぐ}る。
examples.english: To circulate through the blood vessels of the entire body.

examples.japanese: {東洋|とうよう}{医学|いがく}では{血脈|けつみゃく}の{流|なが}れを{重視|じゅうし}する。
examples.english: In Eastern medicine, the flow through blood vessels is considered important.

examples.japanese: {鍼|はり}{治療|ちりょう}は{血脈|けつみゃく}の{滞|とどこお}りを{改善|かいぜん}すると{言|い}われている。
examples.english: Acupuncture is said to improve stagnation in the blood vessels.

notes:
A compound of {血|けつ} (blood) and {脈|みゃく} (vein, pulse, connection). The primary modern usage is the figurative sense of family lineage and hereditary ties. The literal "blood vessel" sense survives mainly in traditional medicine and literary contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {血脈|けつみゃく}を{引|ひ}く: to be descended from, to have the blood of
- {血脈|けつみゃく}を{受|う}け{継|つ}ぐ: to inherit the bloodline
- {血脈|けつみゃく}が{途絶|とだ}える: the bloodline dies out
- {血脈|けつみゃく}を{守|まも}る: to preserve the bloodline

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {血統|けっとう}: lineage, pedigree — often used for animals (horses, dogs) as well as noble families
- {血筋|ちすじ}: bloodline, lineage — more colloquial
- {家系|かけい}: family line, genealogy — focuses on the family tree structure
- {血管|けっかん}: blood vessel — the standard modern medical term (for sense 2)
